Pronunciation note for this grammar point:
The auxiliary is contracted in speech (they'd signed), so the stress falls on the participle when the order matters: they had SIGNED before the audit.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Past Tenses Review.

Build the timeline first: which event is the reference point, which one came before it, which one was in progress. Then choose: reference event in the past simple, earlier event in the past perfect, background in the past continuous, prolonged earlier activity in the past perfect continuous.

past simple — completed events in sequence: they signed in June
past continuous — action in progress, background: they were signing when we arrived
past perfect — earlier event: they had signed before the audit
past perfect continuous — activity continuing before a past point: they had been negotiating for weeks
used to / would — repeated past behaviour: they used to meet on Fridays
past simple after when — interruption of a continuous action: when the call came, we were meeting
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'The train ___ before we reached the platform.'
2. Complete: 'We ___ dinner when the power failed.'
3. Complete: 'They ___ for months before the deal closed.'
Read and listen: three examples in context.

They signed in June. — Single completed event. (Past simple.)
They were signing when the lawyers arrived. — Event in progress. (Past continuous.)
They had signed before the audit began. — Earlier event. (Past perfect.)
What do you observe?

Four past tenses, four jobs. Past simple for completed events in sequence. Past continuous for an action in progress at a past moment, or for the background of a story. Past perfect for an event earlier than another past event. Past perfect continuous for a state or activity that had been going on before a past moment. The time expression usually decides: in 2019, when, before, for months.
1. Which tense marks an event earlier than another past event?
2. Which tense shows an action in progress?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can contrast past perfect and past perfect continuous.

Success criteria:
- I can order past events with the past simple and past perfect.
- I can set a background in the past continuous.
- I can use the past perfect continuous for a prolonged state.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ When I arrived, she already left (past simple for an earlier event) → ✅ When I arrived, she had already left
❌ They were signing the contract before the audit began (continuous for a completed earlier event) → ✅ They had signed the contract before the audit began
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

She opened the file, read the first page and closed it again.
By the time the auditors arrived, the records had gone.
The team had been pressing for a decision since March.
